jobs.title: Graduate Town Planner
jobs.description:
See it differently - Early Careers at Arup

See it differently

You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.

Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.

The Opportunity

Our team does a range of town planning and urban projects including development management, policy development (including strategic planning at strategic authority level) and major sites - we are working on New Towns and do a range of strategic master planning working with multi-disciplinary teams.

As a Town Planning Graduate, You Can Expect To Gain Experience Across a Wide Range Of Sectors And Disciplines, Including But Not Limited To The Following

Preparing applications for statutory consents, including under the Town and Country Planning Act and the Planning Act (2008).

Providing planning policy advice and developing policy, at both local and national level.

Undertaking research and developing evidence bases to support Local Plans.

Undertaking Impact Assessments in support of applications.

Digital planning programmes and research.

Is this role right for you?

For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes:

An undergraduate degree or equivalent qualification in Urban Planning, Geography & Geospatial Science, or Urban Design. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)

Strong research, analytical and written communication skills.

Professional skills: Curious mindset; written and verbal communication; purposeful collaboration.

To Be Considered For a Graduate Opportunity, Your Application Must Include a Copy Of Your Academic Transcript And Meet The Following Criteria

Full working rights in the country of application

No more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role

Recently graduated, or on track to graduate, from your most recent degree, related to your role of choice, before employment starts.

Alongside your degree, we look for the following core attributes;

Changemakers: You care about sustainable development and want to see your work make a genuine difference.
Innovative minds: You think critically, ask hard questions, and are genuinely open to new approaches.
Growth seekers: You are curious, actively seek feedback, and look for ways to keep developing.
Adaptable adventurers: You are comfortable with uncertainty and adapt readily as projects and priorities evolve.

What we offer you

At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.

Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.

We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.

We take an approach to flexible working that supports the diversity and wellbeing of our graduates.

We also provide for our permanent members Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.

Next Steps

We've designed our application process to be straightforward and supportive, giving you the opportunity to showcase your skills and potential. Applications are reviewed as they're received, so we encourage you to apply as early as possible.

The process includes an online application, psychometric testing, application review, case study, interview and offer stage. Our friendly Early Careers team is available throughout the process to answer questions and help you feel confident every step of the way.

Different people, shared values

Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas - this drives our excellence.

Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas.

We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible to all candidates. Please contact UKEarlyCareersRecruitment@arup.com to let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application or interview process, and/or to perform the essential functions of the role. We will do everything we can to support you.

As a Disability Confident Level 2 Employer in the UK, we will strive for one third of all our interview places to be allocated to candidates who have disclosed they are disability confident and best meet the requirements of the role.

Eligibility: Please note that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Therefore, you must ensure that you are eligible to work permanently in the UK without our sponsorship.

Closing Date: Please note, in the event of high applicant volume, this role may be closed ahead of the advertised closing date. Early application is recommended.

jobs.title: Senior Town Planner / Associate Town Planner
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Are you chartered town planner
looking to take the next step in your career by working on some of the UK's most exciting strategic planning, development and infrastructure projects?

We're looking for a Senior Planner or Associate Planner
to join our Planning team in Reading
. This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a leading multidisciplinary consultancy, working on projects that shape communities, support sustainable growth and deliver lasting positive impact.

You'll work alongside experienced planners and technical specialists across transport, engineering, environmental services, architecture, landscape and sustainability, giving you the opportunity to broaden your expertise and play an increasingly influential role in the delivery of complex projects.

Our team works across a diverse portfolio, including strategic land, development management, residential, commercial, mixed-use, infrastructure, regeneration and energy projects. You'll have the opportunity to develop your technical expertise, strengthen client relationships and take greater ownership of projects as your career progresses.

About The Role

As a Senior Planner or Associate Planner
, you'll play an important role in delivering planning projects for a diverse range of clients, while contributing to the continued growth and development of our Reading Planning team.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Managing and contributing to planning applications for a wide range of development projects.
Providing strategic planning and development management advice to clients.
Contributing to strategic planning and plan-making projects across the region and nationally.
Preparing planning appraisals, planning statements, reports and supporting documentation.
Preparing planning appeals including involvement in hearings and public inquires.
Undertaking policy research and monitoring changes in planning legislation and guidance.
Managing project programmes, budgets and delivery to agreed timescales.
Building and maintaining strong relationships with clients, local authorities and key stakeholders.
Working collaboratively with colleagues across multiple technical disciplines to deliver integrated solutions.
Supporting business development activities, including proposals and client presentations.
Identifying opportunities to support the growth of the Planning team and wider business.
For Associate Planner applicants, taking greater ownership of projects, leading client relationships and providing guidance and mentoring to more junior colleagues.
For Associate Planner applicants, supporting the development of the team through knowledge sharing, coaching and contributing to recruitment and wider team initiatives.

Your Impact

You'll contribute to projects that make a genuine difference to the places where people live, work and thrive.

Working across a variety of sectors, you'll help clients navigate complex planning challenges, secure planning permissions and deliver development that supports economic growth, creates new homes, improves infrastructure and enhances the environment.

You'll be part of a genuinely multidisciplinary environment, working alongside specialists across the business to develop integrated solutions and deliver better outcomes for communities and clients.

As your career develops, you'll be encouraged to take on greater responsibility, strengthen your client relationships and contribute to the continued growth and success of our Planning team.

About You

We're looking for experienced planners who are commercially aware, enjoy solving complex problems and are confident building relationships with clients and stakeholders.

You'll Have

A degree, and ideally a postgraduate qualification, in Town Planning or a related discipline.
MRTPI membership.
Significant experience within a planning consultancy, local authority, developer or related environment.
Strong knowledge of the UK planning system, including development management and/or plan making.
Experience preparing planning applications, appraisals, planning statements and technical reports.
Strong report writing, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
The ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work to agreed deadlines.
A collaborative approach and genuine interest in sustainable development.
For Senior Planner level, experience managing planning projects and developing client relationships.
For Associate Planner level, a track record of taking ownership of projects, managing client relationships and supporting or mentoring junior colleagues.

We're particularly interested in hearing from planners with experience across strategic land, residential, commercial, mixed-use, infrastructure, regeneration or energy
, although relevant experience in other areas of planning will also be considered.

Why Join Us

We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. Named ‘Best Place to Work’ and ‘International Consulting Firm of the Year’ at the NCE Awards 2024.
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A p rofessional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered with ICE.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment and Early Careers peer group and wider ERG network (see more on our ERGs here: Stantec Employee Resource Groups )
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the UK & Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, bonus schemes, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard as well as discounted gym membership and lots more.
Flexible working: Enjoy a healthy work-life balance with our hybrid approach to flexible working.

#TownPlanning

About Stantec

The Stantec community unites more than 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across 6 continents. We have been working with our clients and communities in the UK for over 150 years. We plan, design, deliver and manage the development and infrastructure needed to support the creation of sustainable, healthy and prosperous communities.

Our teams provide effective and relevant solutions, translating our clients’ vision into valued consents, deliverable plans for projects and programmes, and efficient designs for delivery, based on technical excellence and deep market insights. We deal with today’s challenges, but also keep a fairer, better tomorrow in sight, looking at how we deliver clean growth, support radical changes in our economy and meet the needs of future communities.

Stantec provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified employees and applicants for future and current employment and prohibit discrimination on the grounds of race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression. We prohibit discrimination in decisions concerning recruitment, hiring, referral, promotion, compensation, fringe benefits, job training, terminations or any other condition of employment. Stantec is in compliance with laws and regulations and ensures equitable opportunities in all aspects of employment.

Building an inspired, inclusive work environment that attracts, supports, and develops world-class talent is a crucial key to our success. If you are excited by this role but worry that your experience doesn’t exactly align, we encourage you to apply.

At Stantec we want you to perform your best at every stage of the recruitment process and are committed to ensuring it is accessible to all. If you need any support or require adjustments to be made then please contact [email protected] and we will talk to you about how we can support you.
